attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps 'magical' and 'waiting in the wings'. The pricing limb is in the present tense, but with 'will pay' and 'will reduce costs' the whole is a firm, undated forward-looking denial, so forecast is acceptable.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: sustainable pricing with real paid adoption, and a deployed advance that measurably cuts serving cost. It rightly treats a price cut or a throughput claim as not enough. Thresholds such as 'at scale' and 'breakthrough' are the evaluator's, which the contract admits.

evidence.note: CoreWeave reports 10x tokens/s per MW over GB200 (July 2026). This is a company disclosure measuring throughput per unit of power, with no full serving-cost accounting, so it does not meet the early-resolution bar.

CoreWeave says Rubin is in limited availability with Cognition in production and 4.8x throughput (Sept 30, 2026). This shows deployment, but it is a company disclosure with no matched cost comparison.

reviews.rationale: This is an undated, firm forecast. Rubin deployment shows real throughput gains, but the packet has only company disclosures, with no verified comparable serving-cost reduction and no sustainable-pricing counterexample. The early-resolution rule is not met. A stretch with no counterexample cannot support the claim. So it is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence. He cites figures from reporting and endorses them in his own argument.

semantics.note: Broadly faithful. 'Well short' paraphrases his framing of the gap between the run rate and the target. It leaves out the 'less than 20%' detail and the 'two-month' trial length, both of which Reuters qualifies (daily exposure, about six weeks).

contract.note: Reading $8.3M as the monthly equivalent of the $100M annualized figure follows his own arithmetic and is fair. Treating 'two months' as approximate and not judging whether the 2026 target is met are reasonable.

evidence.note: Reuters, Mar 26 2026: the pilot crossed $100M annualized within six weeks, and fewer than 20% of users see ads daily. $100M/12 is about $8.3M.
OpenAI's own disclosure backs up the 'more than $100M ARR in under six weeks' milestone. It is a company statement, so corroborating context.

Digiday, Jan 2026, attributes to the FT an expected 'low billions' in ads revenue by year end. This is contemporaneous secondary attribution, which the source requirements allow, and it meets the target limb.
The Feb 9 2026 launch date means the pilot ran about seven weeks by late March, so 'two-month' is a rough description. The pilot was limited to US Free and Go users.

reviews.rationale: Reuters puts the pilot at about $100M annualized, roughly $8.3M a month, and Digiday attributes a 'low billions' 2026 target to the FT. Small imprecisions (six to seven weeks, not two months; under 20% shown ads daily, not 20% of users; the milestone was exceeded rather than hit exactly) do not change the substance. 'Embarrassing' is opinion and is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: The conditional and its antecedent (NVIDIA misses earnings estimates) are kept. 'Crap their pants' is fairly rendered as panic. 'I think ... will' is not on the hedge list. Whether it is hedged does not matter, because the antecedent has not happened.

contract.note: Reading a miss as EPS below consensus, and panic as a broad selloff within a short window, is an ordinary plain reading. The thresholds are the evaluator's, but they do not decide anything here since the condition is unmet.

evidence.note: AP, May 20 2026: NVIDIA beat consensus, adjusted EPS $1.76 against $1.75. This shows the antecedent did not occur. It is not evidence about the predicted market reaction.
MarketBeat, Aug 26 2026: EPS $2.22 against a $2.09 consensus, a beat. Again the antecedent did not occur, and there is no reaction window to assess.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. Both post-publication earnings releases in the packet (May and August 2026) beat estimates, so the antecedent never occurred. Under the policy an unmet condition is not scored. The horizon stays open for future releases.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps 'at some point', the universal claim that none become sustainable, the causal chain, and the broader 'revenue from selling access' wording.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair overall. The metric_scope limits the revenue to what comes from startups, while the revised claim uses broader model-access wording. That mismatch is flagged as an ambiguity and does not affect an unresolved result.

evidence.note: Harvey's gross margin went negative from model costs and then recovered after it moved to its own model. That is gross margin only, not durable sustainability, and it shows adaptation, not death. It neither confirms nor refutes the claim.
Anthropic's S-1 shows consumption revenue growing through H1 2026 but does not isolate startup-derived revenue. Company filing; context only.

reviews.rationale: This is an undated forecast ('at some point'). The packet shows neither broad startup failures caused by model costs with a resulting collapse in lab revenue, nor a verified durably sustainable in-scope startup. Harvey's margin recovery falls short of sustainability. So it is unresolved.
